subject: Request: Nightly job finalization hedge & dedupe plan (SLA amendment request)
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@clearscale.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anne Li <anne.li@clearscale.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Nightly job finalization hedge - impact to SLA and proposed amendment

Hi Tessa,

Quick summary: over the past month we’ve observed our nightly batch thumbnailization jobs (approx. 1.2M items/night) occasionally drifting past our agreed 02:00 UTC finalization window. The drift is intermittent (2–3 times/month) and correlated with longer tail retries after transient GPU preemption on the Dedicated pool.

We’re asking Redwood for a narrow, time-limited SLA amendment to allow a 1-hour finalization hedge for this workload while we implement dedupe/idempotency tokens and safe-retry logic on our side. Concretely:
- Temporary finalization window: 02:00 → 03:00 UTC for nightly jobs for a 90-day period
- Safe-retry expectations: at-least-once allowed during the hedge but Redwood to ensure delivery ordering and provide retry idempotency guidance
- We’re willing to accept a capped service credit if median completion latency exceeds a new threshold.

I’ve attached a sample job history (timeseries) and a short draft SLA amendment (PDF) to start the legal thread. Can you confirm whether this is something Redwood can accept operationally, and what engineering mitigations you recommend so this is not needed after 90 days?

Thanks,
Alex Moreno
Head of Platform Operations
ClearScale Media
(attachment: sample-job-history-2026Q3.csv)

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the artifacts. Looping in Rishi and Marissa for ops + legal.

Quick answers up front:
- We can consider a short-term finalization hedge, but need a technical plan for retry behavior and idempotency to avoid duplicate downstream processing.
- We’ll also want to quantify expected service credits and the gating criteria for reverting to the original 02:00 window.

Rishi — can you review the sample job history and outline a recommended runtime-side safe-retry and dedupe play? Prefer something that avoids global locks and keeps per-request cost low.

Marissa — can you flag any immediate redlines in the attached SLA draft? If we can get a version with acceptance criteria, we can respond to their legal team.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Nightly job finalization hedge - impact to SLA and proposed amendment

Thanks for the details Alex. I dug into the sample CSV — the tail events line up with transient preemptions and occasional backpressure when multiple heavy jobs overlap. Proposed operational approach from Redwood side: 

1) Idempotency token header (recommended): X-Redwood-Idempotency: <client-generated-uuid>
   - If the client includes the same token for retries, Redwood will ensure single application semantics for finalization side-effects (storage writes, webhook notifications).

2) Finalization checkpointing: we’ll persist per-job finalization state (job_id, last_sequence_applied, final_status) with a TTL of 120 days to support dedupe and safe replays. This keeps the runtime consistent while avoiding global locks.

3) Retry/backoff guidance: exponential backoff with jitter, max 6 retries. For long-running bulk jobs recommend chunked checkpoints every 5k items so retries replay smaller windows.

4) Monitoring hooks: we’ll expose a per-job trace id and a finalization webhook that posts when a job reaches terminal status. This gives you deterministic visibility and a single canonical source-of-truth for completion time.

Operational constraints: we can enable a temporary 60-minute finalization hedge for the ClearScale nightly job but we require the client to adopt idempotency tokens and chunked commits within 30 days of amendment execution. Without those, we’ll need a narrower hedge or additional credits to cover dedupe remediation.

I’ve attached a short example of how the idempotency header is accepted and a sample webhook payload (inline below). Let me know if you want Redwood to also provide a small SDK helper to generate and attach tokens from your side.

— Rishi
Principal Engineer, Inference Runtime

Hi Alex — thanks for the draft. From a contract perspective we are open to a 90-day operational carve-out, provided: 

- Acceptance criteria are explicit (e.g., <5 incidents/month causing >30m overrun during hedge)
- Clear rollback criteria (both parties agree when to terminate the hedge early)
- Service credit schedule is defined and caps total liability for the period
- Implementation milestones: idempotency adoption, chunking, and acceptance tests completed within 30 days

I’ve redlined the attached PDF with inline comments. Please let us know if you can accept the milestones and the acceptance tests — we’ll then route an updated amendment for signature.

Marissa Cole

Redwood Inference

Tessa/Marissa/Rishi — thanks for the fast turnaround and detailed plan. ClearScale accepts the operational constraints and milestones:
- We’ll add the X-Redwood-Idempotency header in our ingestion client and switch to chunked commits (5k items/chunk) within 21 days.
- We accept the 60-minute hedge for 90 days, with rollback if acceptance tests (to be scheduled) show tail under control.
- We propose the service credit be a percentage of the monthly committed capacity fee, capped at 10% for the amendment period — happy to take your counterproposal.

I’ve attached a signed redline (simple acceptance) — Anne is on copy for any legal follow-ups. Once you confirm the monitoring webhook field names we’ll add the idempotency header and run a smoke test against the non-prod endpoint.

Best,
Alex Moreno
